title: Multi-country Employment Wave 5M jurisdiction and cross-border data research boundary

researchLeads.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023
researchLeads.notes: Section 16 governs processing of personal data outside India when in force. India Code records sections 3-17, including section 16, in the eighteen-month commencement tranche from 13 November 2025; Wave 5M must not treat section 16 as an operative transfer rule as of 10 August 2026. Any later country-pair pack must re-check effective dates and any higher-protection Indian law.

researchLeads.title: Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025
researchLeads.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
researchLeads.notes: Current MeitY rules and enforcement-timeline material must be re-verified at the time a country pair is selected. Registration here is research context only and not cross-border transfer approval.

researchLeads.title: EPFO International Worker / Social Security Agreement current guidance
researchLeads.notes: EPFO current guidance identifies multiple bilateral Social Security Agreements and country-specific detachment rules. No SSA, certificate-of-coverage route, exclusion or contribution outcome may be selected until the country pair and exact agreement/administrative arrangement are controlled.

researchLeads.title: Income Tax Act, 2025 non-resident and residency guidance
researchLeads.notes: Current guidance states that the Income Tax Act, 2025 governs residential status for tax years beginning on or after 1 April 2026. Residency, source, withholding, treaty relief, permanent-establishment and payroll consequences remain country-pair and fact specific.

researchLeads.title: Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025
researchLeads.notes: The Act is in force from 1 September 2025 and covers visa and foreigner-registration powers. Wave 5M does not select a visa/work-authorisation route or accept passport, nationality, visa or immigration case data.

requiredCountryPairResearchDomains: mandatory employment law and local worker protections
employing entity, payroll entity, secondment and local registration model
immigration, visa, work authorisation and foreigner registration
individual and employer tax, residency, withholding, treaty and permanent-establishment risk
social security, bilateral agreement, certificate-of-coverage and benefit coordination
payroll, currency, remittance and local reporting controls
worker classification, agency, EOR/PEO and contractor boundaries
termination, collective rights, dispute forum and mandatory process
privacy, controller/processor roles, cross-border transfer, localisation and data-subject rights
security, access, retention, deletion, incident and vendor/subprocessor controls

hardBlockers.requirement: Select exactly one supported country pair and record the business operating model before any law/source pack is created.
Obtain qualified employment-law approval for both jurisdictions and the interaction model.
Obtain legal/privacy/security approval for the intended cross-border employee-data flow, roles, locations, vendors, access, retention and transfer mechanism.
Acquire exact current official immigration, visa, work-authorisation and registration sources for the selected pair.
Acquire exact current tax, residency, withholding, treaty, payroll and permanent-establishment sources for the selected pair.
Acquire the exact bilateral SSA/administrative arrangement or record that no applicable agreement exists; do not infer from the EPFO country list.
Acquire exact current employment-law sources for both jurisdictions, including mandatory local rights, termination/process and dispute routing.
Fingerprint the exact approved official files and create source/section mappings only after the pair is selected.
Design and approve an organisation-level fact boundary before assessment capture; person-level mobility, payroll, tax, immigration and case data remain prohibited.

prohibitedData: employee, worker, contractor or dependant identity
personal contact details or home address
nationality, citizenship, passport or travel-document details
visa, immigration, work-authorisation or foreigner-registration identifiers or case content
tax identifiers, tax returns, residency-day counts or travel itinerary
UAN, social-security account numbers, certificate-of-coverage bodies or contribution histories
payroll rows, wages, compensation, bonus, equity or benefit amounts
bank, remittance, currency-conversion or payment data
medical, disability, injury, death, insurance, nominee or dependant information
employment, assignment, secondment, EOR/PEO or contractor agreement bodies
disciplinary, termination, grievance, claim, litigation, notice or order content
precise employee location or movement history
cross-border transfer logs tied to an identifiable person
evidence bodies or uploaded case documents
nextControlledAction: Select one country pair and operating model, obtain specialist jurisdictional plus cross-border data approval, then create exact country-specific source packs and a privacy-safe organisation-level fact contract before any runtime work.
